# Retrospective: PR #12804

## What worked

Bounded security intake covered linked issue context before reviewer launches. Fresh Opus 5.5 High and Sol Xhigh identities and arguments were verified. Independent investigation exposed a mistaken PR premise: bootloader indices include directories. Source evidence resolved the material boot question without unsafe firmware experiments. Original reviewer reports and the explicit peer-informed correction were preserved separately.

## Friction and corrections

A partial clone has enough checked-out head source but not necessarily base blobs. Read-only GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH prevented incidental object mutation; full GitHub patches supplied the three-file comparison. Future source preparation should explicitly materialize needed baseline blobs before inspection if a local full diff is needed.

Sol initially treated an accurate text rewrite as a boot-selection improvement. Synthesis corrected this through upstream indexing source, not simulated text tests. Its initial enrollment suggestions remain local rather than inflate the public finding count.

The first multi-file bash -n attempt checked only the first script. Separate isolated syntax runs corrected coverage; no all-files success was claimed from that initial invocation. Read-only parse/hash/missing-path errors were preserved in native history and excluded from evidence. These were process mistakes, not boundary failures. A fixture's migration-level statuses and source-traced errexit do not constitute separate records of every backend child status, so no fully guarded universal-coverage claim is made.

No Omadev issue was encountered because no desktop resources were used. No boot VM was requested because source inspection answered the important conclusion; more substitute experiments would not improve the public claim.

## Privacy and resources

Public draft contains only public source links and generic product paths/names. Internal evidence and native identities remain private audit material. Native CLI history may store public policy/source and synthetic logs outside the intentional artifact root; history was preserved. No owned long-running runtime process remains: the isolated cases terminated synchronously, and no nest or host service was started. Reviewers remain idle in their owned panes. HTML was saved without opening it.
comment:
The change to `default_entry: 1` selects a directory rather than the first kernel in Omarchy's standard generated Limine menu.

## Entry 1 is the Omarchy directory, so automatic boot stops

Limine counts the expanded parent directory as an entry. For the layout shown in #12664, the source-derived mapping is:

```text
Limine index    Generated menu
1               /+Omarchy          <- PR default: directory
2                 //linux-omarchy  <- existing default: first kernel
3                 //linux          <- retained stock kernel
```

Limine v12 converts the configured number to a zero-based index, [counts the directory before its children](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.0.0/common/menu.c#L909-L937), and [disables the countdown when the selected entry is a directory](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.0.0/common/menu.c#L1545-L1575). The same behavior is present in v11. The generated `/+Omarchy` layout therefore needs index `2` to select its first kernel, not index `1`.

**Impact:** Both the template change and the migration's `2 -> 1` rewrite cause this standard layout to wait for manual kernel selection instead of booting automatically, unless a remembered or one-shot selection overrides the configured default. Unattended reboots can consequently stop at the boot menu.

**Suggested change:** Retain `default_entry: 2` for this layout and remove the migration that changes it to `1`. The stock-kernel symptom in #12664 needs a separate diagnosis of the actual generated order and any selection overrides; its root cause was not established by this review.

**Verified:** Isolated synthetic checks confirmed that the migration rewrites `2` to `1`, preserves `3`, and propagates a simulated top-level enrollment failure. Those checks establish text-editing and failure-routing behavior, not correct boot selection.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Reviewed `cf392d7`. Menu behavior was traced through Limine v11/v12 and entry-tool source. No firmware boot, real ESP update, signing, or native enrollment was tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium coordinated the initial inspection and evidence synthesis; Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh completed independent technical assessments, followed by source-based adjudication and a fresh Astra Medium editorial check.
